import pandas as pd
pd.set_option('display.width',300); pd.set_option('display.max_columns',50)
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
df['dt'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'], format='%m/%d/%y')
# all resources whose price changes on 10/20 or instances jump
for fam, g in df.groupby('instance_family'):
    g=g.sort_values('dt')
    pre=g[g.dt<pd.Timestamp('2025-10-20')]; post=g[g.dt>=pd.Timestamp('2025-10-20')]
    if len(post)==0: continue
    pc = post.price.iloc[0]/pre.price.iloc[-1] if pre.price.iloc[-1] else 0
    ic = post.num_instances.iloc[0]/pre.num_instances.iloc[-1]
    if abs(pc-1)>0.01 or abs(ic-1)>0.5 or pre.price.nunique()>1:
        print(fam, g[['csp','cloud_service','application']].iloc[0].to_dict(), 'price',sorted(g.price.unique()),'inst pre',pre.num_instances.tolist(),'post',post.num_instances.tolist())
print()
w=df.pivot_table(index='instance_family',columns='dt',values='unblended_cost',aggfunc='sum')
pre=[c for c in w.columns if c<pd.Timestamp('2025-10-20')]
d=(w[pd.Timestamp('2025-10-20')]-w[pre].mean(axis=1)).sort_values()
print('most negative deltas:'); print(d.head(10).round(2))
print('total anomaly delta:', round(w[pd.Timestamp('2025-10-20')].sum()-w[pre].mean(axis=1).sum(),2))

steps.content:
I've identified the drivers. Total daily cost jumped from ~25.7k to 27.39k (+1,676 vs 10/19; +1,780 vs the prior 10-day mean). Breaking that down at the most granular resource level (`instance_family`, one row per resource per day, cost = price × num_instances × 24):

| Resource | Context | Before (10/10–10/19) | 10/20 | Δ vs baseline | Cause |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `QD9Fr0KXz9` | GCP / ZfOgd / app 0QF | 7–10 instances, price 1.6322 flat, ~$274–392/day | 49 instances → $1,919.47 | **+1,598.25** | Instance count jump 9 → 49 (~5.4×) |
| `Jg50IWfSz0` | AWS / 6mBxV / app 2m9 | 18 instances @ 0.45 = $194.40/day (flat) | 18 @ 1.50 = $648.00 | **+453.60** | Unit price jump 0.45 → 1.50 (commitment 10/20/24–10/19/25 expired) |
| `IXI4IjtplF` | AWS / 6mBxV / app aig | 17 @ 1.35 = $550.80/day (flat) | 17 @ 0.45 = $183.60 | **−367.20** | Price *drop* (new commitment 10/20/25) — savings, not a cause |

All other 899 resources move only by their normal day-to-day noise (≤ ~$13 each). The two increases (+1,598.25 + 453.60 = +2,051.85) net of the −367.20 saving plus noise explain the entire anomaly. The negative-cost-change resource is excluded since it reduced cost.

Both root causes persist through 10/21 and 10/22, confirming they are step changes rather than noise.
